audit_findings.title: Operating earnings and capital claims use different acquisition perimeters
audit_findings.magnitude: filed six-month Building Systems adjusted EBITDA of $167.3 million and income before tax of $72.0 million, versus the $170.0 million annual OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: The full acquisition debt and acquisition-issued shares enter the bridge and share denominator, but the anchor OE largely represents the legacy Communications business.
audit_findings.evidence: The Building Systems segment reflects the results of Power Solutions following the acquisition on December 23, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated. Power Solutions contributed almost a full anchor's worth of adjusted EBITDA in six months, so excluding its normalized owner earnings is reasonably capable of changing the equity-value scenarios, including moving base equity above zero. EBITDA is not owner earnings, so the precise valuation correction remains unquantified.
audit_findings.action: Build pro-forma combined historical OE using Power Solutions operating cash flow, normalized working capital, cash taxes, and maintenance capital expenditure, then rerun all scenarios with the existing debt and fully diluted shares.

audit_findings.title: Supplier finance may be omitted debt and may have inflated owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $367.4 million outstanding at August 1, 2026; fiscal-2026 accounts-payable cash-flow benefit was $223.2 million
audit_findings.mechanism: If the obligation is financing, it belongs in the equity bridge; any inception-related accounts-payable increase included in cash-flow-derived OE also requires normalization.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company agrees to pay the financial institution the stated amount generally within 60 days of receipt of the invoice.
audit_findings.explanation: The program balance and its exclusion from reported debt are demonstrated, but debt-equivalent classification is unresolved because the filing states that supplier terms are unchanged and payment is generally within 60 days. If treated as debt, the $367.4 million claim exceeds the reported $338 million bull equity value; any unnormalized cash-flow benefit could additionally inflate the OE trend.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the August 1 supplier-level aging, original and program payment terms, and OE workpaper; then rerun with the balance deducted in the bridge, the inception cash-flow benefit removed from OE, or both as supported without double counting.

audit_findings.title: Recurring stock compensation may be added back without matching future dilution
audit_findings.magnitude: filed fiscal-2026 stock compensation of $34.5 million, equal to 20.3% of the $170.0 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash-flow-derived OE can add back noncash stock compensation, while the share denominator captures outstanding awards but not recurring future grants or their replacement cost.
audit_findings.evidence: Each RSU and Performance RSU is settled in one share of our common stock upon vesting.
audit_findings.explanation: Recurring equity compensation and share settlement are demonstrated; the alleged mismatch is not established until the OE workpaper is traced. At 20.3% of anchor OE, however, an omitted recurring employee claim is reasonably capable of materially reducing operating value and altering scenario equity values.
audit_findings.action: Trace stock compensation through every historical OE year and rerun using one consistent treatment: retain the expense, model future dilution, or deduct an equivalent recurring repurchase/replacement-cash charge.

audit_findings.title: Acquired liabilities and earnings remain provisional
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $12.8 million post-closing working-capital adjustment; remaining measurement-period exposure unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Final purchase accounting can change recognized liabilities and the equity bridge, and can retrospectively change depreciation, amortization, or other earnings components used in normalization.
audit_findings.evidence: The purchase price allocation of the company acquired in fiscal 2026 is preliminary and will be completed when valuations for intangible assets and other amounts are finalized within the 12-month measurement period from the respective date of acquisition.
audit_findings.explanation: The August 2026 filing confirms that Power Solutions' allocation remains preliminary and records a $12.8 million adjustment, but the latest balance sheet and cash already reflect known adjustments. The record supplies no range for further liabilities or earnings revisions, so their materiality cannot presently be established.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the final Power Solutions purchase-price allocation to the August 10-Q, identifying all later changes in assumed debt, working capital, contingencies, pensions, indemnities, and cash paid; rerun only bridge or OE items with economic cash consequences.

audit_findings.title: Multiemployer pension withdrawal liability is an unquantified senior claim
audit_findings.mechanism: A probable or economically unavoidable withdrawal liability would be deducted in the equity bridge; higher recurring contributions or surcharges would reduce OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act (“ERISA”), absent an applicable exemption, a contributing employer to an underfunded multiemployer plan is liable upon withdrawal from the plan for its proportionate share of the plan’s unfunded vested liability.
audit_findings.explanation: Participation and potential ERISA exposure exist at the valuation date, but no withdrawal event, liability estimate, or aggregate funding deficit is supplied. Filed contributions of $4.725 million and the green status of one disclosed plan do not measure withdrawal exposure, so the record cannot establish materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain current funding notices and employer-specific withdrawal-liability estimates for every acquired plan, assess expected participation and withdrawal scenarios, and rerun the bridge or OE for supported liabilities or recurring contribution increases.

audit_findings.title: The bridge may deduct net carrying debt rather than creditor principal
audit_findings.magnitude: computed $22.967 million debt understatement, or about $0.75 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Debt issuance costs and original-issue discount reduce GAAP carrying debt but not contractual principal owed to creditors, causing an equal overstatement of equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: The following table summarizes the net carrying value of our outstanding indebtedness (dollars in thousands):
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated bridge error. August principal comprises $1,540.0 million Term A, $800.0 million Term B, $500.0 million notes, and $2.7 million finance leases, totaling $2,842.7 million versus the $2,819.733 million bridge. Correcting it reduces value by about $0.75 per share, only 6.8% of bull equity and 0.26% of market capitalization; base remains negative and bull remains roughly $10.26 per share versus the $287.30 price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each August borrowing to contractual principal and rerun the bridge using $2,842.700 million total principal debt, retaining finance leases consistently.
